title: Preview and Incubating Features
subtopics: Enabling preview features during compilation and execution
Why preview features should not be treated as ordinary stable APIs
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of preview and incubating features and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—meaning of preview features—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study preview and incubating features with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you evaluate upgrades using compatibility evidence instead of assuming every release feature is stable. In this lesson, focus on meaning of preview features and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Check the language/API version, source and target settings, dependency compatibility, and official release notes. A preview feature requires the matching JDK and preview flags and is not a stable production contract. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Compare source, binary, and behavioral compatibility, then run regression tests against the target JDK. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
